answer: We model Sybil resistance as a trellis of repeated identity-registration games wherein each pseudonym stakes a dynamic opportunity-cost bond calibrated to forgone honest yield, serving as the anchor for subgame-perfect punishment matrices that slash misreports in every continuation. Capital barrier analysis proves identity multiplication yields strictly negative expected payoff, since marginal bond costs exceed discounted deviation gains. Adversarial multi-agent convergence then admits a strict Nash equilibrium, the vault of honest play, uniquely trembling-hand perfect.
